facts.text: The library controls basic features of a GE Pressure Automated Calibration Equipment (Pace) controller of models 1000, 5000 and 6000
The core of the library is the Pace object, created with a connection object that provides write_readline and write, in a sync or async version
Module.pressure reads SENS<module>:PRES as a float
The tango server maps pace[1].pressure() to its Pressure attribute with unit bar
Module.barometric_pressure reads SENS<module>:PRES:BAR as a float
Module.pressure_control reads and writes OUTP<module>:STAT as a bool
Module.start() sets the pressure control output of the module True and Module.stop() sets it False
A member read appends '?' to the command; a member write sends '<CMD> <value>;<CMD>?' so the setter is confirmed by a read-back
Pace.__call__(request) sends one request through Pace._query
idn, hw_test, mac, task, error, version, world_area and startup_mode query *IDN, *TST, INST:MAC, INST:TASK, SYST:ERR, SYST:VERS, SYST:AREA and SYST:SET
startup_mode returns a Mode and a float setpoint; Mode.Control is CONT and Mode.Measurement is MEAS
serial_numbers queries :INST:SN1 through :INST:SN7 in one request
The serial number reply maps to ui, ctrl1, ctrl2, ao1, ao2, vfc1 and vfc2 as integers
Module.unit reads and writes UNIT<module>:PRES as a string
Module.pressure_range reads SENS<module>:PRES:RANG through to_name, which strips the quotes
Module.pressure_in_limits reads SENS<module>:PRES:INL
The in-limits reply is parsed as a pressure and a boolean
The tango server reads module 1 for its pressure, source pressure, setpoint, rate, rate mode, control and unit attributes
The tango server publishes pressure control as a bool attribute and writes it with pace[1].pressure_control(value)
The tango server creates the device with connection_for_url(url, concurrency='async') and passes that connection to Pace
Pace._ask appends one newline to the request bytes and uses write_readline for a request that contains '?'
